steps.message: Let me look at EvalHeavy.csproj and what it imports before touching the actual compile step -- evaluation-time cost lives in imports, globs, and property functions, not in targets.

results.content: EvalHeavy.csproj imports imports\level1.props, which imports imports\level2.props, which imports imports\level3.props. EvalHeavy.csproj also declares <AdditionalFiles Include="**\*.*" Exclude="**\bin\**;**\obj\**" /> and a BuildNotes property using $([System.IO.File]::ReadAllText('build-notes.txt')).

steps.message: Three separate evaluation-time costs are stacked here: a three-level nested import chain (level1 -> level2 -> level3), each of which MSBuild has to locate, parse, and merge into the project every single evaluation; a very broad glob (**\*.*) that walks every file under the project directory instead of just source files, which gets expensive fast in a real repo with node_modules/.git-sized trees; and a property function that reads build-notes.txt off disk during evaluation, which is I/O on the evaluation hot path rather than something computed once and cached.

These are all evaluation-phase costs (they happen every time MSBuild parses/evaluates the project, before any target runs), which is a different phase from compilation (CoreCompile/Csc) or incremental up-to-date checks. Recommendations: flatten or reduce the import chain where possible, narrow the glob to something like **\*.cs (or add explicit Exclude for common noise directories), and replace the file-read property function with a value set once via a build property or MSBuild item metadata instead of reading the file on every evaluation.
